title: Fate's Shackles
next_chapter_hook: Mo Xiansheng's words had yet to fall when the Tianji Record suddenly trembled violently, and the shackle runes spontaneously revealed a crack—as if something was attempting to intrude from beyond the rules.

text.content: Night fell ink-black by the cold pool at the Cliff Edge of the Tianqing Sect Back Mountain. Chen Ji sat alone on a cyan stone, the Tianji Record Fragment hovering between his knees, emanating a cold bronze glow. He had sat in this forbidden ground for seven days, studying the fragmented Tianji Record over and over, yet he still could not touch that invisible shackle.

"These shackles... are not a seal." Chen Ji's brow furrowed tightly as his fingertips traced along the patterns at the edge of the Tianji Record. Repeated experimentation over several days had convinced him this was not a simple restriction, but something more intricate... a contract. He closed his eyes and probed his consciousness deep into the Tianji Record, attempting to find clues among those fragmented runes.

dialogue.content: "Every use of the Tianji Record automatically deducts five points of Heavenly Fate... This appears to be a cost, but actually..." Chen Ji suddenly opened his eyes, his pupils contracting sharply. "This is fundamentally the shackles actively absorbing!" He had finally grasped the key he had been overlooking—not that the Tianji Record required consuming Heavenly Fate, but that these shackles were using him as a medium to extract something more fundamental.

text.content: Chen Ji rose abruptly, the Tianji Record in his palm blazing with brilliant light. He plunged his consciousness to the deepest part of that ancient bronze scroll, passing through layers upon layers of rune barriers until he finally reached the core of the shackles. Those were chains as fine as hair, coiling around the Tianji Record's origin, and at the end of each chain hung a faint crimson thread.

"This is..." Chen Ji traced back along those crimson threads, his pupils dilating in that instant. The threads did not originate from him alone but converged from all directions, ultimately pointing toward a direction that chilled him to the bone—the Chen Family Ancestral Land. Each thread connected to a Chen bloodline, and the thickest, brightest one... was linked directly to himself.

The cold pool waters suddenly churned, and a translucent figure gradually materialized from the first page of the Tianji Record. Mo Xiansheng retained his aged, stooped appearance, but tonight his presence felt more ethereal than ever, as if he might dissipate into the night wind at any moment.

dialogue.content: "You've finally found it." Mo Xiansheng's voice trembled like a dying candle flame, carrying an inexplicable sigh. "This old man has waited three hundred years for this moment." His withered finger pointed toward the chains coiled around the Tianji Record. "This is the true nature of the Tianji Record's shackles—not a seal, but a contract."

"In ancient times, your ancestor Chen Wujiu did not merely stumble upon the Tianji Record by chance." Mo Xiansheng paced forward, his ethereal form nearly translucent beneath the moonlight. "He made a bargain with the Heavenly Secrets Palace—exchanging the bloodlines of the entire clan in return for the qualification to inherit the Tianji Record."

Chen Ji remained silent, watching Mo Xiansheng intently. His fist slowly clenched within his sleeve, his knuckles whitening from the pressure. Chen Wujiu... he had encountered this name in Chen family records—a revival ancestor of the clan, revered by later generations as the saint who pioneered the Heavenly Secrets inheritance. So the so-called saint was merely a gambler who struck a deal with mysterious beings.

text.content: Mo Xiansheng seemed to read through Chen Ji's thoughts, shaking his head. "You need not resent your ancestor. Anyone facing such a choice would have made the same decision." His voice grew increasingly ethereal. "That day, the Heavenly Secrets Palace descended and selected the Chen family as candidates for the Tianji Record inheritance. The price was—every generation of Chen descendants would become pieces in the game of destiny, serving for the博弈 of those hidden behind the board."

dialogue.content: "Every generation?" Chen Ji finally spoke, his voice hoarse and unrecognizable. "Those ancestors... those so-called heroes of the Chen family who fell in secret realms, battled demonic tides..." He suddenly laughed, that smile more tragic than tears. "So they were all discarded pieces of the chessboard."

Mo Xiansheng fell silent for a moment, then nodded. "You're clever—clever enough that this old man sometimes feels afraid." He gestured through the air, and those crimson threads suddenly became vivid against the night sky. "See clearly now? Each thread represents a Chen person's life essence. When a thread snaps, death follows; when it dims, decline comes. And the one attached to you..."

text.content: Chen Ji lowered his gaze to his chest, where a faint crimson pattern had somehow materialized, resonating with the shackles on the Tianji Record from afar. The marking glowed fresh as blood, emanating an ancient aura that chilled his heart.

dialogue.content: "You're this generation's Heavenly Fate piece." Mo Xiansheng's voice carried the weight of a verdict. "Those so-called abilities to foresee three hours ahead and reverse destiny—merely sweet rewards the chess master has tossed your way. The true purpose is to have you advance far enough on destiny's board, until..." He paused, as if debating whether to continue.

choice.prompt: Truth lies within reach—how should Chen Ji respond?

choices.description: "Until what? Speak clearly." He stared directly at Mo Xiansheng. Since he was already a piece, he might as well see the entire chessboard clearly.
choices.visible_cost: Face the brutal impact of truth
choices.visible_reward: Grasp the complete rules of destiny's game
choices.risk_hint: The truth may prove far more despairing than imagined

text.content: Mo Xiansheng gazed at Chen Ji for a long moment before finally sighing. "Until your Heavenly Fate is depleted and you perish, your cultivation destroyed. The instant you die, the Tianji Record will automatically return to the board, awaiting the next piece." He paused. "You believe you're changing your fate? No—you're merely walking step by step toward an inevitable end."

choices.description: Chen Ji lowered his gaze, abandoning his questions. Some answers, once known, become burdens.
choices.visible_cost: Temporarily abandon understanding the full picture of the truth
choices.visible_reward: Keep trump cards hidden, not allowing Mo Xiansheng to see through his true thoughts
choices.risk_hint: Mo Xiansheng might hold back because of this

text.content: Mo Xiansheng gazed at Chen Ji's suddenly calm expression, his brow furrowed slightly. This youth's reaction was far too composed—nothing like someone who had just learned they were a piece in the game of destiny. "Aren't you going to ask?" he countered. Chen Ji merely shook his head gently, tucking the Tianji Record into his chest. "Some things, asking won't change. Better to think about what comes next."

choices.description: "Since you know all this, why still help me?" Chen Ji's gaze sharpened. Which side was this remnant soul truly standing on?
choices.risk_hint: Mo Xiansheng's attitude may determine the depth of future cooperation

text.content: Mo Xiansheng froze for a moment, then let out a desolate laugh: "Good lad, you truly haven't disappointed this old man." His form became slightly more solid. "I help you because I too am a piece discarded by that chessboard. When Chen Xuan passed the Tianji Record to you instead of me on his deathbed, he planted a thread of variability within this deadly game."

Night wind rose suddenly, scattering the thin mist around Mo Xiansheng. His silhouette under the moonlight grew increasingly ethereal, as if he might dissolve into the endless darkness at any moment. The surface of the cold pool rippled with layers of waves, reflecting both the countless stars and Chen Ji's expressionless face.

dialogue.content: "The rules of the destiny chess game are simple." Mo Xiansheng continued, "There are three chess players—Heavenly Dao Will, the Destiny Card holder, and... the piece itself. Heavenly Dao Will is the banker, the Destiny Card holder is a thief stealing rules through the cracks of the board, and you—" he pointed at Chen Ji, "are the core... placed right in the center of the chessboard."

Chen Ji suddenly spoke: "Since I'm a piece, do I have the right to choose?" Mo Xiansheng fell into a long silence before slowly shaking his head: "The tragedy of a piece is that what you think is a choice is merely a move anticipated by the chess player. If you wish to jump off the board..." He suddenly paused, his gaze deepening, "Only by becoming a chess player yourself."

choice.prompt: How to understand the meaning of these words?

choices.text: Question the flaws in the chessboard
choices.description: "Since Destiny Cards exist, it proves the chessboard itself is not impenetrable." Chen Ji said coldly, "I will find that flaw."
choices.visible_cost: May trigger the chessboard rules' backlash
choices.visible_reward: Obtain new clues about the Destiny Cards
choices.risk_hint: Mo Xiansheng may warn you not to act recklessly

dialogue.content: "Destiny Cards..." A strange glint flickered in Mo Xiansheng's eyes, "You've indeed already encountered those things." He suddenly lowered his voice, "Indeed, the chessboard has cracks, otherwise I wouldn't exist. But those cracks are limited—every touch will accelerate the tightening of the shackles."

choices.text: Ask how to become a chess player
choices.description: "What are the conditions for becoming a chess player?" Chen Ji's eyes burned with intensity—if there was a path, he would walk it to the end.
choices.visible_cost: Mo Xiansheng's answer may be despair-inducing
choices.visible_reward: Clarify the ultimate goal of future cultivation

dialogue.content: Mo Xiansheng shook his head bitterly: "If this old man knew, I wouldn't have been trapped in this fragment for three hundred years." His voice carried the weight of time, "But before Chen Xuan died, he said something — 'On the chessboard, all are pieces; only by transcending the chessboard can one become the player.' Perhaps the method to transcend lies within the complete version of the Tianji Record."

choices.description: "Heavenly Will... is it watching us now?" Chen Ji suddenly asked a question that even made Mo Xiansheng's expression slightly change.
choices.visible_cost: May expose that one has already sensed the existence of the Tianji Record
choices.visible_reward: Obtain a warning about the Heavenly Eye
choices.risk_hint: The Heavenly Eye may have already noticed you

dialogue.content: Mo Xiansheng's face changed drastically. He abruptly looked up toward the Void, as if searching for something. After a moment, he slowly withdrew his gaze, his expression toward Chen Ji becoming more complex: "You... actually already know?" Chen Ji did not answer, simply watching him silently. Mo Xiansheng was silent for a long time before finally sighing: "It is everywhere, but we still have time. As long as the shackles remain unbroken, it cannot directly interfere."

text.content: Chen Ji was silent for a long time before finally speaking again: "Over these three hundred years, how many Chen family descendants have reached the same step as me?" Mo Xiansheng did not answer, but his evasive gaze said everything. Chen Ji suddenly laughed, his laughter echoing by the cold pond in the silence, carrying an indescribable sorrow: "So what I thought was defying fate to change destiny was merely repeating the same pattern."

The cold pond's water suddenly boiled, countless bubbles surging from the depths as if something was awakening. Mo Xiansheng's face turned pale: "Not good! The shackles are sensing your emotional fluctuations!" He waved his hand, a surge of spiritual energy pushing Chen Ji several zhang away, "Calm down! Your anger is feeding it!"

Chen Ji felt the blood-red pattern on his chest pulsing frantically, and an immense power was seeping into his body along the thread connecting to the Tianji Record. It was an indescribable sense of oppression, as if an invisible eye was watching him through the shackles, wanting to see through everything about him.

choice.prompt: Facing the shackles' strange movements, Chen Ji must make a choice:

choices.description: Chen Ji took a deep breath, pressing all his anger and unwillingness into the deepest part of his heart. He could not lose control here.
choices.visible_reward: The shackles temporarily calm down, gaining a moment to catch one's breath
choices.risk_hint: Suppressed emotions will erupt at some future moment

text.content: Chen Ji's breathing gradually stabilized, and the blood-red pattern on his chest slowly weakened. Mo Xiansheng exhaled: "Good, good. Being able to stay calm in this situation, you are stronger than any generation this old man has seen." His figure grew increasingly ethereal, "Remember this feeling — turning anger into calculation is how a piece survives."

choices.text: Go against the current, perceive the source
choices.description: Instead of passively taking hits, better to actively trace the source. Chen Ji probed deeper along that blood-red thread with his divine sense.
choices.visible_cost: May trigger more severe restrictions from the shackles
choices.visible_reward: Sensed a trace of abnormality at the source of the shackles
choices.risk_hint: This abnormality may become the key to breaking the situation

text.content: Chen Ji's divine sense went against the current, passing through layers upon layers of bloodline barriers, finally arriving at the source of those shackles. There, he saw a scene that made his entire body go cold — at the end of the shackles, connected to nothing mysterious, but rather a pair of eyes watching this place. Cold, lofty, utterly without emotion — it was the Heavenly Eye.

Those eyes slowly opened in the Void, coldly observing Chen Ji's divine sense. Without words, without pressure, merely this observation itself made Chen Ji feel dizzy, as if all his secrets were being seen through by those eyes. That was not the gaze of a chess player examining pieces, but rather... the gaze examining ants.

dialogue.content: "Enough!" Mo Xiansheng roared, his remnant soul suddenly erupting with dazzling light, forcibly severing the connection between Chen Ji and those eyes. Chen Ji collapsed to the ground, cold sweat soaking his back. Mo Xiansheng's figure had already faded to near transparency, his voice weary: "You were too reckless... Had it been a moment later, the shackles would have completely devoured your divine sense."

text.content: Chen Ji sat on the cold blue stone, gasping heavily. That glimpse of terror had deeply carved itself into his soul—that was an existence surpassing his understanding, the true Heavenly Dao that viewed all things as mere chess pieces. Mo Xiansheng's form swayed precariously, yet he forced himself to speak: "Remember the appearance of those eyes—that shall be your ultimate enemy."

"I understand." Chen Ji slowly rose to his feet, his voice already restored to its usual calm. "So that's how it is... I thought I was struggling against fate, but in truth, I was merely thrashing about under its gaze." He raised his head to gaze at the night sky—the starlight was dim, as if something was drawing near. Mo Xiansheng's form grew increasingly illusory, yet he still struggled to maintain his shape: "But at least now you know the truth. A chess piece that knows the truth might find the possibility of breaking the game."

Chen Ji lowered his gaze to the Tianji Record in his palm. The binding runes on that ancient bronze scroll were pulsing slightly, as if resonating with something. He suddenly spoke: "Those fate cards... can they break these chains?" Mo Xiansheng's form trembled, seemingly hesitating whether to answer this question. After a long while, he finally said: "Fate cards are fragments stripped from the chessboard's rules... theoretically, perhaps there exists a possibility."

Before Mo Xiansheng could finish speaking, the Tianji Record suddenly shuddered violently—the binding runes actually manifested a hair-thin crack on their own. Mo Xiansheng's expression changed drastically, and Chen Ji's pupils constricted—the诡异的气息 from beyond this world was seeping out from that crack, as if something was attempting to break in from outside the rules.
